units: <cite ref="Shabbat 150a:1">Sabb. 150ᵃ</cite> (play on <he>מ̇ד̇ה̇ב̇ה</he>, v. <cite ref="M00251">preced.</cite>) <he>מ̇אד̇ מ̇אד̇ ה̇ב̇א בלא מ̇'</he> bring much, very much, without measure.
<cite ref="Mishnah Peah 8:6">Peah VIII, 6</cite> <he>מ׳ זו</he> this proportion.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 64">Gen. R. s. 64</cite>; Esth. R. introd. (ref. to <cite ref="M01712"><he>מנדה</he></cite>, <cite ref="Ezra 4:13">Ezra IV, 13</cite>) <he>זו מִדַּת הארץ</he> that is the tax from the land as measured, i.e. the (Roman) land-tax.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 7:3">B. Bath. VII, 3</cite> <he>מ׳ בחבל וכ׳</he> I sell thee exact land-measure by the rope.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 128a:8">Ib. 128ᵃ</cite> <he>מִדַּת ארכו</he> the length-measure of the cloak.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 128a:8">Ib.</cite> <he>מדת משקלותיו</he> the measure of its (the gold-bar’s) weights, i.e. an estimate as to how many coins of a certain weight can be obtained from it.
<cite ref="Chagigah 12a:5">Ḥag. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>מדת יום ומ׳ לילה</he> the combined length of day and night.
<cite ref="Yevamot 76b:14">Yeb. 76ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="I Samuel 17:38">I Sam. XVII, 38</cite>) <he>מַדָּיו כמִדָּתוֹ</he> his (Saul’s) garments such as fitted his stature.

<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 10:5">Mikv. X, 5</cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 73a:2">Ḥull. 73ᵃ</cite> <he>עד מקום</he> (<cite ref="E00000"><he>ה</he></cite>)<he>מ׳</he> as far as the designed length of the handle (excluding the portion which it is intended to cut off).—
<cite ref="Kiddushin 42b">Kidd. 42ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Metzia 56b">B. Mets. 56ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>דבר שבמ׳ ושבמשקל וכ׳</he> objects which are sold by measure, by weight or by the piece.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 89b:11">B. Bath. 89ᵇ</cite> <he>לעולם … מ׳ חסירה וכ׳</he> one must never keep in one’s house too small or too large a measure (smaller or larger than the legal size); a. fr.—Pl. <he>מִדּוֹת</he>, <he>מִידּוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 88b:6">Ib. 88ᵇ</cite> <he>עונשן של מ׳</he> the divine punishment for fraudulent measures.

Tosef. B. Mets. VI, 14 לא היו ממונין … אלא על המ׳ they (the agoranomoi in Jerusalem) were appointed not for the regulation of market prices but for the superintendence of the measures; B. Bath. 89ᵃ, v. אֲגַרְדְּמִיס; a. fr.—
Men. 18ᵃ למצות מִידּוֹתַי, v. מָצָה.—Whence: Middoth (measurements of the Temple), name of a treatise of the Mishnah, of the order of Kodashim.

senses.gloss: dealing; reward or punishment; dispensation.—מ׳ כנגד מ׳ retaliation, adequate punishment or reward.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 1:7">Sot. I, 7</cite>, v. <cite ref="M00251">preced.</cite>
<cite ref="Sotah 9a:4">Ib. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>לכמ׳</he> the verse is to intimate the God dispenses adequate punishments.

<cite ref="Sotah 8b:12">Ib. 8ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 1:7">ib. I, 7</cite>) <he>אע״ג דמ׳ בטילה במ׳ לא בטיל</he> although retribution (by the Jewish court) has ceased, the adequate divine punishment has not ceased. Lam. R. introd. (R. Alex. 2) (expl. <he>יען וביען</he>, <cite ref="Leviticus 26:43">Lev. XXVI, 43</cite>) <he>מ׳ כנגד מ׳</he> punishment corresponding to deed.
<cite ref="Nedarim 32a:12">Ned. 32ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 90a:19">Snh. 90ᵃ</cite> <he>כל מִידּוֹתָיו של הקב״ה מ׳ כנגד מ׳</he> all retributions of the Lord are in correspondence with man’s doings.

<cite ref="Berakhot 48b:6">Ber. 48ᵇ</cite> ‘whatever the Lord thy God has given thee’ <he>דיינך בכל … בין מ׳ טובה ובין מִדַּת פורענות</he> (not <cite ref="M00252"><he>מדה</he></cite>) he is thy judge in whatever sentence he decrees upon thee, whether it be a good or an evil dispensation.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 9:5">Ib. IX, 5</cite>, v. <cite ref="M00005"><he>מְאֹד</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 97a:2">Sabb. 97ᵃ</cite>.
Ib. 151ᵇ לעולם … על מ׳ זו at all times let one pray to be spared this fate (poverty); a. fr.—Pl. as ab.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 90a:19">Snh. 90ᵃ</cite>, v. supra.

<cite ref="Yoma 87b:1">Yoma 87ᵇ</cite> <he>המעביר על מִדּוֹתָיו וכ׳</he> he who passes over his retaliations (who forbears to retaliate), his failings will be passed over (be forgiven); <cite ref="Megillah 28a:21">Meg. 28ᵃ</cite>.
Ib. לא עמדתי על מִידּוֹתַי I never insisted on retaliation; Kidd. 71ᵃ ואינו מעמד על מדותיו (Rashi: מעמיד); a. fr.—3) manner, ways, character, nature, condition.
<cite ref="Berakhot 40a:14">Ber. 40ᵃ</cite> <he>לא כמדת הקב״ה וכ׳</he> the nature of divine (intellectual) affairs is not like the nature of human (material) affairs.
<cite ref="Berakhot 11b:14">Ib. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>להזכיר מדת יום וכ׳</he> to mention the nature of the day (light) at night. Tanḥ. Balak 3 <he>מה מִדָּתוֹ</he> what is the nature of his power.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 33a:18">B. Mets. 33ᵃ</cite> <he>מ׳ ואינה מ׳</he> it is a (meritorious) way (of studying) and is not, i.e. you might to better; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 3:5:9">Y. Hor. III, 48ᶜ</cite> top <he>מ׳ שאינה מ׳</he>; a. fr.—Pl. as ab.

<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:10">Ab. V, 10</cite> <he>ארבע מ׳ באדם</he> there are four different dispositions of men (as to treating one’s fellowman); <cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:11">ib. 11</cite> <he>ארבע מ׳ בדעות</he> four characters (temperaments); <cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:12">ib. 12</cite> <he>ארבע מ׳ בתלמידים</he> four natures of students (with regard to receptive and retentive faculties).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 11:3:5">Y. Snh. XI, 30ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>כל שבע מ׳ וכ׳</he> all the seven characteristic features of righteous men which the scholars have defined have been realized in Rabbi.
<cite ref="Nedarim 20b:8">Ned. 20ᵇ</cite> <he>בני תשע מ׳</he> children conceived under nine (abnormal mental) conditions.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 17b:2">R. Hash. 17ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>שלש עשרה מ׳</he> the thirteen divine attributes (<cite ref="Exodus 34:6">Ex. XXXIV, 6</cite>, sq.).
<cite ref="Nedarim 32a:12">Ned. 32ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="Q01744"><he>פָּרַז</he></cite>; a. fr.—<he>מדת הדין</he>
Tosef. Yeb. IX, 3. a. e., v. לָקָה.—Esp. the divine attribute of justice, opp. מ׳ הרחמים, v. דִּין II.—
senses.label: a

units: <cite ref="Yoma 43b">Yoma 43ᵇ</cite> <cite ref="K00655"><he>כך</he></cite> (<he>היא</he>) <he>מ׳ הדין נותנת</he> common sense dictates this; <cite ref="Shevuot 14a:2">Shebu. 14ᵃ</cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 2:1:16">Y. Maas. Sh. II, 53ᶜ</cite> top <he>תחומין עשו</he> (<he>כמ׳</he>) <he>למ׳ הדין</he> they regulated the laws of Sabbath limits according to common sense (not by textual interpretation).—
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: decision in money matters, civil law (contrad. to ritual law).
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 5:1:9">Y. Gitt. V, 46ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>אף למ׳ הדין הכן</he> the same principle holds good for civil law (collection of claims, v. <cite ref="K01058"><he>כַּפְרָנוּת</he></cite>); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 10:2:3">Y. Shebi. X, 39ᶜ</cite> bot.

<cite ref="Yoma 2a:8">Ib.</cite> (last line) <he>ולמידין מ׳ הדין וכ׳</he> do we apply the rules of Prosbol (v. <cite ref="Q01646"><he>פְּרוֹזְבּוּל</he></cite>) to ordinary claims? <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma 5:1:2">Y. B. Kam. V, beg. 4ᵈ</cite> <he>לא הילכו במ׳ הדין אחר הרוב</he> (strike out <he>בממון</he>) in civil law we are not guided by probabilities (v. <cite ref="D00171"><he>דוֹב</he></cite>; cmp. Bab.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 27b">B. Kam. 27ᵇ</cite>). Y. Ber. II, 5ᵃ bot. <he>ולמ׳ הד׳</he> but civil law (questions of possession).
senses.label: c

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 3:4">Men. III, 4</cite> <he>כמדת ר׳ וכ׳</he> following the principle of R. &c.; <cite ref="Pesachim 77b:15">Pes. 77ᵇ</cite>; Y. ib. VII, 34ᶜ top.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 4:6">Shek. IV, 6</cite> <he>אינה היא המ׳</he> (comment. <he>אינה מן המ׳</he>) this is not consistent (with a previous rule).
<cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 4:7">Ib. 7</cite> <he>השוה את מִדָּתוֹ</he> (Y. ed. <he>מִדּוֹתָיו</he>) he makes his standards even (is consistent).
<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 1:7">Pes. I, 7</cite> <he>אינה היא המ׳</he> this is not the right argument.
<cite ref="Pesachim 15b:15">Ib. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>אמאי אינה היא המ׳ מ׳ ומ׳ היא</he> why do you say, it is no argument? it is surely a correct argument.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 3:2:9">Y. Ḥag. III, 77ᵈ</cite> ‘Menahem went out’ means <he>ממ׳ למ׳ יצא</he> he went over from one principle to another (joined the opposition; Bab.

ib. 16ᵇ יצא לתרבות רעה).—Esp. מִדּוֹת rules of interpretation. Sifra introd., ch. I, end הלל … שבע מ׳ וכ׳ Hillel the Elder explained seven rules &c.; Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXXVII; Tosef. Snh. VII, 11. Sifra introd., beg. (R. Yishm. said) בשלש עשרה מ׳ וכ׳ the Torah is interpreted by means of thirteen rules. [Appendix to treat. B’rakhoth. ל״ב מ׳ של ר׳ יוסו וכ׳ the thirty two rules of R. José the Galilean.]—
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 3:7">Lev. R. s. 3</cite>, beg. <he>הלכות ומ׳</he> decisions and interpretations (by which the decisions were reached), v. <cite ref="M01379"><he>מְכִילְתָּא</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Gittin 67a:9">Gitt. 67ᵃ</cite> <he>מִידּוֹתַי תרומה מתרומות מִידּוֹתָיו וכ׳</he> my rules of interpretation are the selection from selections of rules by R. Akiba.—

<cite ref="Berakhot 33b:17">Ber. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>שעושה מדותיו של הקב״ה רחמים וכ׳</he> he makes compassion the standard (or reason) of the divine laws, while they are decrees (the reasons for which it behooves not man to discuss); Y. ib. V, 9ᶜ <he>כקורא תיגר על מ׳ וכ׳</he> because it sounds as if he were finding fault with the ways of the Lord (as if the Lord were partial); <he>כנותן קיצבה למ׳ וכ׳</he> as though he were setting limits to the attributes of the Lord.
